rootText: Settling Down Settling down looks different for everyone – you could be getting married, buying a home, or trying for your first child. But one thing’s for certain: you’re planning to safeguard the life you’re creating and its future. Contact us Build Your Security As You Build Your New Life Consider your priorities for you and your family and make a plan to build a bright future for everyone. Protection HIGH PRIORITY In the event of unexpected circumstances such as critical illnesses, accidents, or death, you and your loved ones’ needs and livelihood might be affected. Your priority for protection: Health insurance for hospitalisation. Protection against accidents and major illnesses so that your needs during recovery continue to be met. Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability. Maternity insurance if you’re planning for children. Plan your protection Wealth HIGH PRIORITY You have likely taken on more financial demands such as a wedding, home mortgage, future children’s education, and retirement. Your priority for wealth: Savings for immediate and future expenses. Retirement planning. Contact us Protection Safeguarding your health grows in importance as you embark on a new phase of life. Saving for your upcoming milestones will be easier when you don’t have to worry about medical expenses. What you already have1 If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability. What you may consider2 With big-ticket items lined up in your future, being sufficiently protected is critical in ensuring that your savings can be used as intended – for the new life you’re building. National schemes do not fully cover: Hospitalisation An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Critical Illness You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)3 Death & Total and Permanent Disability You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)3 Savings2 To stay covered and accumulate savings over the years. Maternity Coverage for baby and mum. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection. Why Act Now Health crises can cause income loss and depletion of family funds2. Ensure either partner can sustain the family if the other faces an unfortunate event. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. My life insurance coverage only needs to be twice my annual salary. Health insurance is only for old people. I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Misconception: My life insurance coverage only needs to be twice my annual salary. Truth: In general, it’s recommended to have 9-10X your annual earnings as basic life coverage. However, this amount can vary depending on your family expenses and desired legacy, so it’s best to consult with a Financial Representative who can give you a plan that fits your needs. Source: 2022 protection gap study – Singapore, Life Insurance Association Singapore, 8 September 2023 Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Health insurance is only for old people. Truth: Health issues and accidents can happen to anyone at any age. While older people might be more prone to certain illnesses, it's important for everyone to have health insurance. If you wait until you're older, insurers might exclude pre-existing conditions. Protect yourself by getting coverage early on. Source: Understanding Health Insurance, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Truth: While this is true, it is also true that health issues can arise at any time, regardless of age. It’s also wise to lock in a lower premium at a younger age.* Yes, I want an expert’s help Find The Right Plan Savings Investments Achieve your life goals at any life stage and gain financial security and the freedom to live out your best years. Contact us Wealth Making plans to settle down requires stability. Having a plan to grow your money steadily will help achieve your goals including future expenses and retiring comfortably with your partner. Basics – what you should have3 Emergency Funds At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days. Legacy Planning A plan for a will, family trusts, life insurance, powers of attorney, and CPF nominations. What you may consider2 Creating new memories during your new phase of life will need savings. Giving your money time to grow can mean that your future milestones can be met comfortably. Investment It is recommended to allocate at least 10%3 of your take-home pay for key milestones. A Retirement Plan3 It is never too early to start building your nest egg for the retirement lifestyle you want, including monthly payouts. Why Act Now Supporting dependants and your lifestyle requires building a well-diversified portfolio2. As lifespans are increasing4, you’ll need a plan for your financial needs in the future. Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Investing is risky. You need to be knowledgeable about the market to invest. I should always buy term life insurance and invest the difference. Misconception: Investing is risky. Truth: Investing does come with some risk, but there are ways to manage it. You can balance risk and potential returns by diversifying your investments and choosing lower-risk assets. Understanding your own risk tolerance and considering your financial commitments are also important in reducing investment risk. Source: Managing Investment Risk, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: You need to be knowledgeable about the market to invest. Truth: While investing will indeed be easier and less risky if you have at least some basic knowledge, you don’t need to be an expert in the field to start. Understanding your risk appetite, future goals, and potential risks is a good start. Speak to a Financial Representative to learn more and understand how to balance your risk appetite with your financial goals! Source: What to Ask When Buying An Investment Product, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: I should always buy term life insurance and invest the difference. Truth: There are pros and cons to both! While term life insurance do charge relatively lower premiums, investing the difference yourself means taking on all the investment risks. It may also result in insufficient coverage in old age. Understand your financial goals, assess your situation, and talk to a Financial Representative to make the best decision for you.
